articles.content: The CDU/CSU party is debating whether to keep its strict rule against working with the far‑right AfD. While some eastern CDU members want a softer approach, the party leaders, including Friedrich Merz, say the rule will stay unchanged.
articles.title: The debate over the immigration limit within the conservative bloc continues to simmer.

articles.content: Negotiations between the governing parties on changing the military service have broken down, and a planned press conference was cancelled. Members of the SPD party opposed a proposed lottery that would pick people for service if there are not enough volunteers. Because of this, it is still unclear whether the new law will be presented to parliament.
articles.title: Agreement on military service apparently failed at least for now.

articles.content: The German government wants to add about 80,000 soldiers and plans that young men born from 2008 must give a readiness statement and could be called up if there are not enough volunteers. Some politicians suggest using a lottery to decide who must serve, but legal experts say this may clash with the constitution’s rule of fairness. The matter could be decided by the constitutional court.
articles.title: Is a lottery procedure legally permissible?
